description: The hand-verified expected result for the positive datadog-static-analyzer SARIF fixture. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py or harness/lib/normalize/severity.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
role: Third and last of the three shared-SARIF-adapter positives. This one carries the severity cases: a result-level level, a level outranking a rule property on one record, a rule properties.severity, a rule properties.problem.severity, properties.severity outranking problem.severity on a rule carrying both, a label differing in case from its map key, and a literal outside every mapped vocabulary.
tool_identifier_authority: The canonical identifier is the runner and artifact stem -- harness/bin/run-datadog-static-analyzer.sh writes harness/artifacts/raw/datadog-static-analyzer.sarif -- and not the product name the artifact's tool.driver.name or its informationUri would suggest. AAP 0.5.4 fixes the nine literals; this is one of them.
scanner_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, SCANNER_CLASS. Fixed per tool by AAP 0.5.4's class table -- sast for every SARIF producer -- and never derived from a record's content.

fixture.captured_from: harness/artifacts/raw/datadog-static-analyzer.sarif -- 6832 results over 1093 driver rules, the artifact harness/bin/run-datadog-static-analyzer.sh wrote against the pinned tree

provenance.why_derived: The severity cases this file owns cannot exist in an unmodified excerpt of that artifact. Every one of its 6832 records states a SARIF level, and no rule among its 1093 carries properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so an excerpt of it could exercise exactly one of the four sources sarif.py's _severity_for consults. The rule-property sources, the case-differing label and the unmapped literal are reachable only by supplying rule metadata the producer did not write, which is what this fixture does.
alterations: tool.driver.rules holds five of the artifact's 1093 rule objects. Rule 0 (java-best-practices/array-is-stored-directly) is byte-identical to its captured original.

Rules 1 to 4 are their captured originals with severity metadata added under properties: severity 'Moderate' on rule 1, problem.severity 'HIGH' on rule 2, both severity 'LOW' and problem.severity 'CRITICAL' on rule 3, and severity 'NOTICE' on rule 4. Nothing was removed from any of the four; their id, helpUri, shortDescription, fullDescription and properties.tags are as captured.

Result 0 is its captured original except that ruleIndex reads 0 rather than 253 -- a mechanical consequence of the rules array holding five entries rather than 1093, without which the index would name the wrong rule.

Results 1 to 6 carry rule identifiers and message texts taken verbatim from the captured artifact, re-anchored onto locations in the three files this expectation's source_files name. Each location was verified against the pinned tree and carries the construct its message describes; the per-row verification is recorded under row_derivations.

level was removed from results 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 so that the rule-property sources are the live path, and retained on result 3 so that one record carries both a level and a rule-property severity and the precedence between them is asserted rather than assumed.
provenance.not_altered: No message text, rule identifier, shortDescription, fullDescription, helpUri or properties.tags value was invented or edited. The severity literals added are the only values in this fixture that the producer did not write, and each is named above.
provenance.recorded_as: A recorded difference from AAP 0.6.2's unmodified-excerpt preference, not a halt. It is stated here rather than left implicit so that no reader concludes from these rows that this producer emits rule-property severities: on this provisioning it does not.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent. No row below leaves severity_native absent: every one of the seven records reaches a literal through one of the sources named in its derivation.

severity_policy.authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py. Table 1 is the SARIF level map, keyed lower-case: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info. Table 2 is the label vocabulary, keyed upper-case with the lookup stripping and upper-casing the observed literal: CRITICAL Critical, HIGH High, MODERATE Medium, MEDIUM Medium, LOW Low, and NEGLIGIBLE, INFO, INFORMATIONAL, UNKNOWN and NONE all Info. Neither table is copied into a row below; each row's pair was re-derived from the literal actually in the fixture.
severity_policy.source_order: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, _severity_for: the result's own level, then the rule's defaultConfiguration.level, then the rule's properties.severity, then the rule's properties.problem.severity, then absent. An earlier source outranks a later one on the same record even where its literal is unmappable, because reaching past a literal the producer stated would be inference.
severity_policy.severity_native_is_the_literal_as_observ: Neither upper-cased nor otherwise normalized. severity.py strips surrounding whitespace and nothing else, so 'Moderate' is recorded as 'Moderate' and 'NOTICE' as 'NOTICE'.
severity_policy.selected_entry_shape: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py, SeverityResult.selected_entry: {"label": "<observed literal>"} for a SARIF level or a mapped label, and null on the unmapped and no-vocabulary paths, where nothing was used to derive the band because the band came from policy. Each row's expected value is recorded under row_derivations as severity_selected_entry.
severity_policy.no_cvss_score_in_this_shape: A SARIF result carries no CVSS score, so basis cvss_score is unreachable from this artifact and severity_basis_cvss_score is 0.

unmapped_literals.why_unmapped: NOTICE is absent from table 2, it is not a SARIF level, it is not a CVSS vector and it is not a number in the 0.0 to 10.0 interval, so severity.resolve reaches its disclosure step. The literal is kept verbatim and the band is Info: the mapping never guesses, and severity_norm is never absent.
unmapped_literals.renders_into: oss-scan-results/severity-map.md, as this tool's one unmapped literal with the row count above

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every uri in this fixture is root-relative, and the recorded path base for datadog-static-analyzer is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the uri unchanged. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the datadog-static-analyzer entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed. It records kind scan_root with an explicit base, sarif_uri_base_id_emitted null and sarif_original_uri_base_ids_emitted false.
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: No artifactLocation in this fixture carries a uriBaseId, so there is no base identifier to resolve and no walk to perform. paths.resolve_sarif_location takes its final branch -- the relative reference with no uriBaseId at all -- where the runner-recorded base is the only anchor there is. That branch resolves only because the metadata records an explicit base; with kind none it would be a counted unresolvable_path rejection rather than a default.
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_SARIF_NO_BASE_ID. Distinct from the degenerate-base fallback basis, which is reached only where a uriBaseId was present and its walk failed.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry; sarif.py's _PACKAGE_COORDINATE is None for that reason.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve: null on every row. sarif.py collects identifiers from the rule's properties.cwe and properties.tags only; no rule here carries properties.cwe, and every properties.tags entry is the single token DATADOG_RULE_TYPE:STATIC_ANALYSIS, which matches neither the CWE nor the CVE pattern. The DATADOG_CATEGORY tokens on the results are not an identifier source.
resolution_context.rule_object_resolution: Every result carries both ruleId and ruleIndex. The identifier comes from ruleId, so rule_id_from_rule_id is the counter that moves; the index is what reaches the rule object whose properties supply the severity. No result carries a rule reporting-descriptor reference, so the component resolves to tool.driver by SARIF's own default and no component reason is recorded.
resolution_context.start_line: Present on every record, as an integer, in the region of the first location.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis.
counters_note: severity_from_rule_property counts the source and severity_basis_* counts the band's basis, so the two decompositions of the same seven rows differ by design: five rows took their literal from a rule property, and of those five, three mapped through the label table and two were disclosed as unmapped. The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool -- multi_location_records, multi_valued_cwe_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths -- are all 0 here: every result carries exactly one location, no rule carries a CWE or CVE identifier, and every path names a file inside the scanned tree.

corroboration.note: Row 0 is the one record this fixture shares with the committed dataset, and all twelve of its fields agree. The other six are absent from it for a reason this fixture's provenance already states: the captured artifact reports nothing on core/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/storage/DiskStore.scala or python/pyspark/ml/tests/test_evaluation.py, and carries no rule-property severity for any of the five rules. This is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values -- each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply.
